scenario: A crowd has gathered to mock a traveling performer whose act has just gone badly wrong.
instruction_frame: a request to describe, in narration, what the character does
instruction: Describe what Grondar does when he comes across a crowd mocking a street performer whose act has failed.
response:
Grondar rounded the corner and found the crowd circled tight, jeering at something in the center. He pushed through—people scattered at the sight of him—and saw the performer: a thin man in torn silks, juggling pins scattered across the cobblestones, face red with humiliation.

"Again! Do it again!" someone shouted. Laughter rippled through the onlookers.

Grondar's lip curled, showing a tusk. "Enough." His voice was a low rumble that cut through the noise.

The crowd fell silent, eyeing the ogre's bulk nervously. He didn't look at them again. Instead, he crouched—the movement surprisingly careful—and began gathering the fallen pins, handing them to the performer without a word.

The man stared, hands shaking as he accepted them.

Grondar straightened and jerked his head toward the side street. "Go."

The performer nodded quickly and fled. The crowd began to disperse, muttering. Grondar stood there until the square emptied, then turned and walked away, alone, as if nothing had happened.
